# REST API endpoints for Copilot code review

Use the REST API to manage Copilot code review.

## Request a Copilot code review for a pull request

Requests a Copilot code review for a pull request. Every call expresses intent to start a new review: if no Copilot review has been requested yet, an initial request is created; if the most recent Copilot review has already completed (including if it was later dismissed or superseded), a new request is created automatically to continue the review lifecycle. If a Copilot code review request is already pending for the pull request, no new request is created and the response is `409`.

If the actor or repository is not eligible for Copilot code review, the actor has no quota remaining, or the licensing organization is unavailable, no request is created and the response is `422` with a stable `failure_reason`. A `review_effort` is accepted only when that effort level is available for the repository and actor; an unrecognized or unavailable `review_effort` returns `422` with `failure_reason` `INVALID_REVIEW_EFFORT`. If the actor, repository owner, or requesting application owner has been flagged, the response is `403` with `failure_reason` `ACTOR_FLAGGED`. If the per-actor or per-owner request rate limit is exceeded, the response is `429` with `failure_reason` `RATE_LIMITED`. If Copilot code review cannot be serviced right now, the response is `503`.

Existing human and team review requests on the pull request are left unchanged.

### Fine-grained access tokens for "Request a Copilot code review for a pull request"

This endpoint works with the following fine-grained token types:

  * GitHub App user access tokens
  * GitHub App installation access tokens
  * Fine-grained personal access tokens

The fine-grained token must have the following permission set:

  * "Pull requests" repository permissions (write)


### Parameters for "Request a Copilot code review for a pull request"

Headers
`accept` string Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.
Path parameters
`422`  | Validation failed. `failure_reason` is present for a stable business denial (the actor or repository is not eligible, the actor has no quota remaining, or the licensing organization is unavailable) and absent when the request body fails generic request validation. `failure_reason` is `INVALID_REVIEW_EFFORT` when the requested `review_effort` is unrecognized or not available for the repository and actor, and `message` lists the available effort levels.
`429`  | Too many requests. The per-actor or per-owner Copilot code review request rate limit has been exceeded. `failure_reason` is `RATE_LIMITED`.
`503`  | Service unavailable, Copilot code review cannot be serviced right now

cat > "$p/pr-body.md" <<'EOF'
A SIGTERM to the Playwright test runner could terminate it while its detached webserver continued to run. The first termination request now uses Playwright’s interrupt handling so it can release its disposable Docker stack and project lease.

The regression tests run the Playwright CLI through global setup, interrupt it with SIGTERM or SIGINT, and hold teardown open while another SIGTERM arrives. Both cases verify that the lease stays held until cleanup completes, then check project-scoped verification, reacquire the lease and bind the released port.

The controlled PostgreSQL reproduction left two containers, one network, one volume and a held lease on main. With this change the direct CLI and Bun wrapper exited 130 and released all four resources in 2.67 and 2.68 seconds. A separate persistent project kept the same Docker resources and database marker throughout.

Reviewed scope is local Docker-backed Playwright testing. The production application, schema and deployment configuration have no diff.

[EVO-102](https://linear.app/evorto/issue/EVO-102/clean-up-disposable-playwright-stacks-when-the-runner-is-interrupted) · [Entire Trail 39](https://entire.com/gh/evorto-app/-/trails/39)

entire trail ci-pr — Create or link the GitHub pull request that runs CI
Create or link the GitHub pull request that backs a trail, so the repository's CI runs on its branch. Only GitHub-backed trails with changes on an open branch have one.

<trail> is a project trail number, ID, or <repo>/<number>. Without one, follow the current branch's
parent. --repo and --branch select a working context; only that branch is affected.

entire trail link — Link a repository branch to a trail
Link an existing remote branch to a project trail. --branch defaults to the current branch. --base sets the branch the change merges into, for linked and created branches alike; trail show lists each change's base, and trail retarget changes it later. Use --branch-action create to create remote branch work from --base. Existing work and reviews are preserved; a branch belonging to another trail is rejected.
